Because the full text is not provided, I cannot verify whether any exclusion criteria (e.g., use of rest-only baseline, ROI-only analyses, non-healthy participants) are met or violated. Therefore I must exclude due to incomplete/full-text unavailable for full verification. Inclusion IDs met: I5. Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Exclusion IDs met: none (cannot determine)." ,

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-Back) in healthy adults (mean age 31.8), reporting within-participant contrast (2-Back > 0-Back). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and coordinates/thresholds are reported; results are presented in text, figures, and tables. Imaging modality (BOLD fMRI), sample demographics, and task paradigm are described. Supplemental material is referenced but not required for core criteria. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visuo-spatial working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (3 participants, ages 30–32). It reports within-participant contrasts (delay-phase WM vs control task) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (SPM2 analyses; significant clusters reported with stereotaxic coordinates, P<0.05 corrected). Imaging modality and task paradigm are described (1.5T T2*-weighted EPI, vsWM delay-response task), and participant health/ages are provided. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state-only, not non-empirical, and participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of prospective memory and working memory (executive function/cognitive control). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., PM-1Back vs NB-1Back; NB-3Back vs NB-1Back), uses group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with whole-brain results and cluster thresholds (tables/figures/coordinates reported), and provides participant demographics confirming a healthy adult sample (ages 19–29). Tasks fall within executive function domains (working memory, sustained attention/monitoring). Imaging modality is fMRI and full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults and reports within-participant contrasts (instruction type, memory load). It reports participant ages, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm. However, the paper reports results primarily as ROI analyses (FFA, PPA, dorsolateral PFC) with no clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps presented; therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task of executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts between task conditions), I9 (working memory task), I10 (participant age/health/modality/task reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI task study of negative priming (an inhibition/executive control paradigm) in healthy adult participants (ages 22–28). It reports within-subject task contrasts (NeuI > C, NegI > C, NegI > NeuI) and group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates (tables/figures). Imaging modality, participant health/age, and task paradigm are clearly reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adult bilinguals that explicitly investigates cognitive control processes (translation requiring inhibition of the dominant language and language switching requiring set-shifting/phonological recoding). It reports within-subject contrasts (translation vs reading; switching vs no-switching) using group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with tables of coordinates. Participant ages (25–39), healthy status, imaging modality (PET), and detailed task paradigms are reported. The tasks map onto established executive function domains (inhibition, cognitive flexibility). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses active control baselines, empirical human neuroimaging with healthy adults aged 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Given these points, the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a PET task-based neuroimaging study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults. It includes a within-subject contrast of the self-ordered working memory task versus an active control task, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and statistical thresholds, and provides participant age, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (an executive-function domain) that: (1) uses a task-based paradigm probing manipulation/maintenance (WM) versus an active control condition (three Xs/button press) and reports within-participant contrasts ([load − control]); (2) reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and stereotaxic coordinates and figures; (3) provides sufficient participant information (healthy control group demographics, imaging modality, task details) and examines healthy controls separately; and (4) clearly falls within established executive function domains. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group healthy participant activations). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults.

This task-based PET study in healthy adults (n=6, ages 19–32) assesses conditional movement selection (stimulus-response mapping), a form of cognitive control/response selection. It includes a within-subject contrast of conditional versus active control tasks (conditional − (power+precision)/2), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with peak coordinates and t-values, and provides participant demographics, healthy sample confirmation, imaging modality, and task details. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses fMRI to assess an executive function task (verbal 2-back working memory; I5, I9); includes within-participant contrasts of task vs an active baseline (symbol discrimination) allowing task-evoked contrast (I6); reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and random-effects group analyses with stereotaxic normalization and correction for multiple comparisons (I7) with results presented in figures/tables (I8); and provides participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task details (I10). The healthy control group provides within-group activation maps appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive-function activations in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-only baseline, or age-range violations). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study tested working memory (delayed recognition) for voice identity and location — an established executive function domain (working memory). It reports within-participant contrasts of each memory task versus an active sensorimotor control, and direct voxelwise group-level whole-brain statistical maps (Z-maps) with tables/figures and ROI analyses. Participant age (18–27), healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain task activation maps; not connectivity-only; includes within-group contrasts; uses an active control; healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study includes a 2-back working memory task (an executive function domain) with within-subject task block modeling and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Z-statistic maps, cluster-corrected). Participant age range (22–52), healthy status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. The 2-back task used alternating task and control epochs including an active control (‘TAP’ response epochs), and the GLM produced whole-brain activation estimates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, not resting-state-only, empirical human data, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (delayed-recognition of kinesthetic hand movements), which falls within executive function (working memory). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., Set 3 > baseline) against an active control (circular patterns). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise SPM results with coordinates and thresholding reported. Participant information (healthy adults aged 20–28), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so full-text is complete.

This fMRI study of healthy adults (ages 21–35) examines spatial working memory (an executive function domain) using a task-based within-subject contrast (memory-guided saccades vs visually guided saccades), i.e., an active control comparison. The paper reports group-averaged, whole-brain results and Talairach coordinates (voxelwise activation maps summarized in group data/tables), describes imaging modality (3T fMRI), participant health/ages, and task paradigms in sufficient detail. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. The provided full text includes intro, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI, task-based, within-subject study that explicitly contrasts tool-planning (TOOL-NOGO) versus an active control (CONTROL-NOGO), reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with coordinate tables, and investigates planning — an executive function domain. Thus it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the provided full text does not report participant ages or age ranges (it reports only 'healthy adults' and sample sizes/handedness), and the review's I10 requires that relevant information about participant age be reported. Because I10 is not satisfied in the provided content, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria and is therefore excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text is judged complete for the purposes of screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=30, mean age 30) using a task that falls squarely within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports within-participant, task-based contrasts (e.g., WM/DMS correct vs incorrect and subsequent memory contrasts) analyzed in a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM and presents coordinates and figures of whole-brain results. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. There are no violations of exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, does not use rest/fixation as sole baseline, is empirical with original human neuroimaging data, and participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an event-related fMRI study manipulating verbal working memory load (HOLD vs RELEASE) in healthy adult participants (fMRI n=10, mean age 26.1). The design includes within-subject contrasts of task conditions (HOLD vs RELEASE) addressing working memory, an established executive function domain. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed with SPM and reported (thresholds, coordinates, tables/figures described), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, empirical data in healthy adults).

Full text appears incomplete (only title and abstract provided). Based on available information: imaging modality is PET and task is verbal fluency (an executive initiation task), so I5 and I9 are satisfied. However, key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed: I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control) is unclear—while multiple tasks are reported, it is not explicit that an active control contrast was used; I7 (group-level whole-brain/voxelwise results) is not verifiable from the abstract; I10 (reporting of participant ages and full participant details) is incomplete—the abstract only states “four normal subjects” with no ages. No exclusion criteria are clearly met from available text, but because the full text is incomplete, we cannot determine eligibility. Exclude for now due to incomplete/full-text unavailability and unmet/uncertain inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I10.

This is an fMRI study of working memory updating (an executive function) in healthy adults that reports within-subject contrasts (multiple updating-load conditions vs 0-load and a memory control task), group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinate tables and figures, and participant/sample, imaging modality, and task details. The experimental contrasts constitute active control comparisons (0-arrow with visual fillers; separate memory control task). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the supplied full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This fMRI study meets the inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI engaging executive processes via the reverse-alphabetizing WM/manipulation task), I6 (within-participant contrasts between Alpha and retrieval tasks), I7 (whole-brain, group-level ST-PLS results reported with tables/figures), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures), I9 (task engages working memory/executive control), and I10 (participant ages, healthy screening, imaging modality, and task paradigms reported). However, it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes participants older than 60 years (older group ages 62–80), so the study includes participants outside the 18–60 healthy adult range required by the review. Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite satisfying the inclusion criteria. Inclusion IDs not met: none.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (N=17, ages 18–30) that uses a delayed match-to-sample working memory paradigm (executive function domain: working memory). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of DMS (working memory) versus active control (CON) tasks (e.g., DMS delay > CON delay), and performs group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise statistical maps and reported coordinate tables/figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task details are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control using a spatial Stroop conflict paradigm (executive function: inhibition/conflict resolution). It reports within-subject contrasts (informative cue vs neutral cue; P–N, W–N, P–W) and group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates and thresholding. Participants are healthy adults (n=14 after exclusions), ages 18–32. Imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Excluding because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the available content. Inclusion criteria met based on provided information: I5 (fMRI study; authors state they used functional magnetic resonance imaging and keywords include working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast: bilateral vs unilateral conditions reported), I9 (task relates to working memory/executive domain as indicated in keywords and interpretation). Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be confirmed: I7 (no explicit confirmation in the provided content that a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map was produced or reported), I10 (participant age information not reported—only “seven normal volunteers”—so cannot confirm ages within 18–60 and other participant details). No exclusion criteria from the specified list are explicitly met. Because the full text is incomplete and essential methodological details cannot be verified, the study is excluded pending full-text availability.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level task activations in a within-subject design in healthy adults (mean age reported, n=15 analyzed). The task includes decision-making under provocation and contrasts against control (computer) trials, yielding contrasts probing cognitive control/conflict monitoring (dorsal ACC) and reward-related decision processes. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses and stereotaxic coordinates are reported (tables/figures). Although the primary aim is reactive aggression, the paradigm elicits and measures cognitive control/conflict monitoring and decision processes that map onto executive function (cognitive control/inhibition/conflict monitoring) and thus satisfy the review’s scope. All required reporting elements (modality, participants, task, coordinates) are present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, active control present, healthy adults 18–60). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study examines preparatory brain states and cognitive control mechanisms (ACC) during problem solving and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise contrasts (insight vs noninsight), but the provided full text does not report participant age information required by inclusion criterion I10. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study of cognitive control/executive processes), I6 (within-participant contrasts of task conditions), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text), I9 (task involves cognitive control/cognitive flexibility relevant to executive function). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (participant age not reported in the provided full text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered by the available information. Full text appears complete for methods/results/discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 24–32) reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses comparing self-selected (free selection) actions with observed actions. The self-selection condition involves executive processes (response selection, working memory/maintenance, attentional selection) and was contrasted within-subject against an active control (observation condition). Methods report whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with thresholding and coordinate results. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion E8 applies: the study includes participants with fragile X syndrome (a clinical/non-healthy group) and is not restricted to healthy individuals, so it does not meet the review’s requirement for studies of healthy adults only. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function: switching/inhibition), I6 (within-participant contrasts for control participants using task event types), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported using SPM99), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I9 (task falls within executive function domains), I10 (participant ages, healthy-control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract: the paper is an fMRI methods paper that used an oddball paradigm and a block working memory task to illustrate a model for removing global signal confounds. Inclusion criteria met/verified: I5 (fMRI task-based study using working memory) and I9 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory). Inclusion criteria not met or not verifiable from available text: I6 (no clear within-participant contrast vs an active control is reported), I7 (no evidence of group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps), I8 (no whole-brain results/coordinates reported in abstract), I10 (no participant age/healthy-sample confirmation or detailed imaging/task reporting). Exclusion criteria met: none confirmed (E7 methods-only cannot be established from abstract alone). Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E6: the working memory (executive function) task appears to use rest/fixation (long ISIs) as the baseline rather than an active control condition, and no within-participant contrast against an active control condition is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI including a working memory executive task), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory), I10 (participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no evidence of a within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion. Consequently the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly tests top-down/intentional control over encoding and retrieval (executive/cognitive control). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing high-intention (remember/recognize) vs low-intention (look/re-view) conditions, which serve as active control conditions. Group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses are reported, with tables of coordinates and activation maps (FDR-corrected). Participant ages (18–31), healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are reported. The task probes initiation/top-down control processes tied to executive function. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting-baseline only, includes healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of task switching (cognitive flexibility/executive function) in healthy adults (n=8, age 20–31). It reports within-subject contrasts (switching conditions vs control and baseline), group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with reported coordinates and figures, and describes participant demographics, imaging modality, and task paradigm. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria for the review (fMRI executive task, within-participant contrasts against active control, group whole-brain maps reported, coordinates/figures provided, task within executive domains, and participant/sample details). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Exclusion: E8 applies — sample age range is 17–25 (includes 17-year-olds), i.e., participants outside the eligible 18–60 range. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study with an executive function task: visuospatial working memory), I6 (within-subject experimental vs active control contrast for the working memory task), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I9 (working memory is an established executive function), I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). No other exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore, exclude due to E8 (age inclusion violation).

This is an event-related fMRI study of a delayed-match-to-sample working memory task in healthy adults (mean age ~25). It reports within-subject contrasts across memory-load conditions (1/3/6 items) and retention/encoding/retrieval epochs, and derives group-level whole-brain voxelwise parametric maps and coordinate tables (Talairach) using SPM99; behavioral and demographic information (healthy sample screening, NARTIQ) and imaging modality (fMRI) are provided. The task is an established executive function domain (working memory). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion E3 met: the primary task activation analyses were anatomically restricted/ROI-based rather than reported as group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps for the executive domain of interest. Inclusion I10 met: participant demographics, healthy sample, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. Inclusion I5 not met: although this is an fMRI task study, the paradigm examines voluntary spatial attention and implicit visuomotor responses (tool vs. non-tool), which do not clearly fall within the specified executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Inclusion I6 not met: there is no within-participant contrast of an executive function task relative to an active control condition as defined by the review. Inclusion I7 not met: no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map for an executive function contrast is provided. Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

This study meets the meta-analysis criteria: it is an fMRI task-based study of an executive function (spatial working memory) in healthy adults, uses within-participant contrasts isolating working-memory (4s delay > 1s delay), and reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise SPM2 analyses with tables/figures of coordinates. Participant age (50–60, mean 56.9), healthy screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. Although sample is small (n=10) and participants are postmenopausal women undergoing hormone/placebo crossover, the required within-subject task contrasts and whole-brain maps are present for inclusion in an activation meta-analysis of executive function. No exclusion criteria were violated.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (2-back vs 0-back) in healthy adults and reports participant details and task paradigm (meets I5, I6, I9, I10). However, the imaging was limited to two contiguous slices covering auditory cortex (not whole-brain), and the analyses are ROI/slice-limited and ICA on transformed limited slices rather than a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Therefore it fails I7 (no whole-brain group-level map) and meets exclusion E3 (only ROI/slice-limited results with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examines spatial working memory and memory-guided saccades in healthy adults and reports whole-brain maps and participant details. However, it does not report a within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control condition; task activation maps are derived relative to fixation/baseline and cyclic mapping rather than an active control condition. Thus it fails inclusion criterion I6 and violates exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline/no active control). Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise mapping and group analyses), I8 (coordinates and maps reported), I9 (working memory = executive function), and I10 (age range, healthy sample, imaging modality, task described). Not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast vs active control). Therefore excluded.

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation of verbal working memory retrieval in healthy adults (mean age ~28) using a task within the executive function domain (working memory). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., Load1 > Control; L2 > L1; L3 > L2; target vs non-target paired t-tests) against an active control condition (motor control trials), and presents group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses with reported coordinate peaks and statistical thresholds (unthresholded and small-volume-corrected results), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Participant demographics, healthy status screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper does not report only ROI analyses, connectivity/resting-state-only analyses, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical work, nor does it include participants outside 18–60 or non-healthy samples. Full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; thus fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an event-related fMRI study of spatial working memory (an established executive function domain). It reports within-subject contrasts between the memory task and an active control task (scrambled faces), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise composite/contrast maps (thresholded images and Talairach coordinates are reported). Participant information (n=12, ages 24–33, healthy), imaging modality (fMRI, 1.5T), and detailed task paradigm are provided in the full methods. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function), reporting within-subject contrasts of the memory task versus an active control (letter case judgment). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM) are reported with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults (mean ages ~23–25), imaging modality is fMRI, and the task paradigm and results are described in methods and results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active control tasks, empirical fMRI data, participants in 18–60 healthy range). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included.

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/metadata and a redirect notice). Based on available information: inclusion criterion I9 (task domain = working memory) is suggested by the title and thus is considered met. However, key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the incomplete content: I5 (fMRI/PET modality assessing executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map), I8 (reporting of whole-brain results), and I10 (participant age/healthy sample and imaging/task details) are not met/confirmable. No exclusion criteria from the list are demonstrably met. Because the full text is incomplete, the study cannot be confidently assessed for eligibility and is excluded pending full-text access. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I10.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–36) that uses task-based paradigms targeting working memory (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., MGS vs SIR; cue, delay, and response epoch contrasts) and group-level surface/voxelwise statistical maps (permutation-based surface maps, with contrasts reported in text and figures). Participant demographics, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting-only baseline, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and can be included in the meta-analysis.

Although this fMRI study uses an executive function task (auditory 2-back working memory) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and figures, it does not include a within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition (e.g., 0-back or another active baseline). The analyses focus on task responses across light conditions and sessions rather than a task vs active control contrast, so inclusion criterion I6 is not met. The study meets I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are directly triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adult participants. It reports within-subject contrasts isolating delay-related working memory processes (intermediate vs short delay; long vs intermediate delay), i.e., task contrasts between active task conditions rather than only rest, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and statistical thresholds. Participant demographics (mean age, handedness, healthy status), imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported in the full text. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function). It reports within-participant contrasts (informative vs. neutral retro-cues; load interactions) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-based thresholding and peak coordinates. Participant age (20–30), healthy status (healthy volunteers), imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses active task conditions rather than rest baseline, empirical human neuroimaging, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (an executive function) in healthy adults (five right-handed males, ages 31.6–37.2). The design includes a within-participant contrast (Incorrect Matching minus Correct Matching) comparing an inhibition condition to an active control, and group-level whole-brain activation maps were computed and reported (thresholded t-maps with Talairach coordinates). The paper reports participant ages, health/selection criteria, imaging modality (fMRI) and task details. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, coordinates) is present. Although sample size is very small (n=5), this does not conflict with the review inclusion/exclusion rules. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a target-detection oddball task that explicitly assesses cognitive control/executive function (target vs novel contrasts isolate task-dependent control). Analyses include within-participant contrasts (shape targets vs novels; face targets vs novels; direct comparison) at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects (FLAME) with reported cluster thresholds and MNI coordinates. Participants are healthy adults with reported ages (19.3–47.5), and the paper reports imaging modality and task details. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates working memory (novel face maintenance) with event-related, group random-effects, whole-brain analyses. It satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts including WM vs LTM and WM delay contrasts), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (results reported with coordinates/figures), and I9 (task falls within executive function: working memory). However, I10 is not satisfied: the full text does not report participant ages or an explicit statement of healthy sample status (only 'volunteers from the student community' and right-handedness are provided). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study is excluded for failure to meet I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=12, age 25–40) examining working-memory/manipulation and central-executive demands using a word-reversal task and rhyme judgment. It includes within-participant contrasts of an executive-demanding task (word reversal) versus an active control task (rhyme judgment) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with tables/figures; ROI small-volume corrections are supplementary. Participant details, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported. The word-reversal contrast engages executive/working-memory-related regions (dorsolateral PFC, bilateral parietal), which map onto established executive-function domains. No exclusion criteria were met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete for screening purposes.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory manipulation (executive function) in healthy adults. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (colour-coded memory-guided saccade manipulation vs baseline fixation and other contrasts), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis (SPM2 and nonparametric SnPM2) with cluster correction, and presents results in figures and tables. Participants (N=13) are healthy adults aged 20–28. Imaging modality, paradigm, and participant details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, and baseline includes an active colour-sequence control rather than passive rest). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of task switching (cognitive flexibility), with healthy adult participants (ages 21–35). It reports within-subject contrasts (switch vs repeat), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures, and detailed methods/results (behavioral, whole-brain contrasts, ROI time-course analyses). All required participant, modality, and task information are reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that tests quantifier comprehension and explicitly contrasts higher-order (WM-demanding) versus first-order quantifiers. It reports within-participant, group-level, whole-brain (SPM99 random effects) voxelwise analyses with coordinates/figures (Table 1, Fig. 1). The higher-order vs first-order contrast taps working memory/executive resources, satisfying the executive-function domain requirement. Participant age, health status, imaging modality (1.5T BOLD fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, active control/subtraction task used, empirical data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: participants are outside the 18–60 age range (mean ages ~72–74) and the sample is not restricted to healthy individuals (includes Alzheimer’s disease patients). The study otherwise meets all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts: EWM > SM), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with corrected statistics), I8 (coordinates and activation tables described), I9 (working memory is an established executive function domain), and I10 (participant ages, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). No other exclusion criteria apply. Because E8 is decisive (age and sample restrictions), the study must be excluded.

This study uses task-based fMRI during mental arithmetic with healthy adult participants (ages 21–35) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses. However, the within-subject contrast is arithmetic versus closed‑eye resting (a rest/fixation baseline). Per the review’s exclusion E6 (rest or fixation as the only baseline without an active control), this violates required control condition criteria and therefore fails inclusion criterion I6 (task contrasted against an active control). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task study), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported), I9 (task falls within working memory/executive domain), I10 (participant demographics and health, modality, and task are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (contrast against an active control). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This PET study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts of metabolic effects of acute ethanol (influx vs placebo, elimination vs placebo, influx vs elimination) and correlates resting metabolic activity with neuropsychological test performance. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I8 (coordinates/tables/figures provided), I9 (neuropsychological tasks include cognitive flexibility/attention), I10 (participant demographics and imaging modality reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (imaging was not a task-based fMRI/PET paradigm assessing executive function during scanning — FDG uptake was measured during rest under infusion rather than during execution of the executive tasks), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control condition — tasks were performed outside the FDG uptake window and no task>control activation contrast is reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are directly triggered. Therefore excluded because essential inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=10, ages 23–32). It uses a Stroop paradigm (inhibition/cognitive control) with within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs neutral) and additional active tasks, satisfying an executive-function comparison. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group average Z-maps, thresholded; Table 1 provides Talairach coordinates) and describe imaging modality and participant characteristics. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This article reports task-based fMRI (concurrent ERPs/fMRI) of an executive function (response inhibition) using an auditory cued go/nogo paradigm (I5, I9). Within-participant contrasts (nogo minus control) are reported (I6). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps and voxelwise t-tests were conducted and reported for the healthy control group (nogo vs control), with thresholding and cluster reporting (I7; descriptions/coordinates/regions provided consistent with acceptable reporting per I8). Relevant participant information (healthy control group presence, matching to patients, age matching described, imaging modality and task paradigm) is provided (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include within-group healthy participant activation maps, use an active control condition (not rest-only), and are empirical human neuroimaging data. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Hence study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

Exclusion E6 met: the study reports task activation contrasted against fixation/baseline (visual fixation cross) rather than an active control task; thus it uses rest/fixation as the primary baseline for the within-participant contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — visuospatial working memory DMTS), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and cluster-wise inference with tables of coordinates), I9 (task falls within the working memory domain), I10 (participant age/health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion I6 is not met: there is no within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition (contrasts are task vs fixation or baseline). Because E6 is violated, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study uses task-based fMRI of an executive function (spatial working memory) with within-subject WM vs active control contrasts and reports whole-brain voxelwise results in healthy volunteers. However, it violates exclusion criterion E8: the healthy sample is outside the target age range (mean age 63.8, >60) and the study includes clinical (schizophrenia) participants rather than being restricted to healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Therefore excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60.

Excluded because the study does not assess an established executive function domain targeted by this review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-subject contrasts: easy/difficult vs active baseline), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with correction), I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures), I10 (participant age, healthy sample, imaging modality [fMRI], and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the study investigates temporal discrimination/timing, not an executive function or cognitive control task per se), I9 (task does not fall within defined executive domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates prediction and frequency-matching and explicitly manipulates working memory (detect 1-back vs detect 3-back). It reports within-participant, within-group contrasts (Predict vs Detect and Predict vs Detect 3-back) using random-effects, whole-brain SPM analyses with coordinates and figures, and provides participant age range, health screening, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigms. No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not a between-group patient study only, not a non-empirical paper, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (verbal working memory n-back) in healthy adults, includes within-participant contrasts (2-back vs 0-back; negative vs neutral), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and statistical maps (SPM2 results, tables and figures), and provides participant demographics confirming a healthy sample within the 18–60 range. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. There are no exclusion criteria met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group activation contrasts, uses active control 0-back, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study of working memory in healthy adults with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps reported; however, the analyses focus on delay-period activity contrasted against baseline/ITI rather than an active control condition. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I9 (working memory task within executive domains), I10 (participant/sample and imaging/task details reported). Inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control condition) is not met. Exclusion criterion E6 is therefore triggered: the study uses rest/blank/ITI baseline rather than an active control condition for the primary contrasts. Full text appears complete. Consequently the study is excluded.

Although this is an fMRI task study that investigates inhibitory control (LPFC involvement) and reports within-participant contrasts across motion-coherence conditions, the provided full text does not report participant ages or explicitly confirm a healthy sample, and it is unclear whether group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables/figures are reported. Therefore required inclusion criteria for whole-brain evidence and participant/sample reporting are not satisfied based on the provided content.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults explicitly probing executive processes (working memory, selective attention, response monitoring) during rule-based versus similarity-based categorization. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with Talairach coordinates (tables/figures), and provides within-participant contrasts (e.g., LOW-DISTORTION vs MEMBER+HIGH-DISTORTION; early vs late learning within each condition) that index increased executive demand. Participant demographics and health status are reported. Thus the paper satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for modality, whole-brain group maps, task-based probing of executive function, within-participant contrasts, and adequate reporting of participants and methods.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Cannot verify key inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none (no sufficient evidence). Inclusion IDs not met / not verifiable: I5 (uncertain whether task is classified as an executive function task — movement preparation may reflect motor intention/planning but this is not clearly framed within established executive domains), I6 (no clear report of a within-participant contrast versus an active control condition in the provided text), I7 (no confirmation of group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps in the provided content), I8 (while results are summarized, qualifying whole-brain results or coordinate tables are not present in the excerpt), I9 (task domain mapping to established executive domains is not clearly demonstrated), I10 (participant age/health status and full task/imaging details are not reported). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm all required criteria; therefore the study is excluded pending full-text review.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study reports BOLD fMRI in healthy controls on a working-memory task (so I5 and I9 are satisfied). However, the available content does not allow verification of: a within-participant contrast vs an active control (I6), a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map (I7), or reporting of participant ages and full sample details required (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) can be confirmed from the available information. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the truncated/full-text information, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

Although this is an event-related fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (I7) and reports results and coordinates clearly (I8), and provides participant/sample/imaging/task information (I10), the experimental paradigm is a sentence-reading/lexical ambiguity language comprehension task rather than an established executive-function or cognitive-control task. The study does not implement or contrast a canonical executive function task (e.g., working memory manipulation, inhibition task, cognitive flexibility) within participants; reading-span is measured as an individual-difference covariate rather than an executed working-memory task. Therefore it fails to meet I5, I6, and I9. No exclusion criteria from E3–E8 directly apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory in healthy adults that reports within-participant contrasts using an active control (no-delay) condition, uses an established executive domain (working memory), and provides participant age/health, imaging modality, and task details. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task assessing executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I9 (task within executive function domain), I10 (participant demographics, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task described). However, the study does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map: analyses were performed and reported at the single-subject level only. Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (group-level whole-brain map) is not satisfied, which is required. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is not met, the study must be excluded.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The abstract indicates a PET study using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task and voxelwise SPM95 analyses, so I5 (PET executive task), I7 (group-level voxelwise maps), I8 (maps/figures acceptable), and I9 (WCST = cognitive flexibility) are met. However, the abstract does not explicitly report a within-participant contrast versus an active control condition (I6 not confirmed) and does not report participant ages or explicit confirmation of a healthy sample (I10 not confirmed). Because not all inclusion criteria can be verified and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending full-text inspection. Exclusion criteria met: none (none clearly violated based on abstract).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory in adults that reports within-subject task-vs-control contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise analyses. However, the sample includes smokers who meet DSM-IV criteria for nicotine dependence, so the cohort is not restricted to healthy participants. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study of executive function/working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), I9 (task = working memory). Inclusion criterion I10 (confirmation of healthy sample status and participant info) is not met because participants include individuals with nicotine dependence despite reporting other medical/psychiatric screening; thus the sample is not exclusively healthy. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI working-memory task with an active control and within-subject contrast, but the reported analyses are ROI-based rather than group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps. Exclusion E3 applies (only ROI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive-function working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I9 (task is working memory). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no evidence of group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map reported), I10 (participant age not reported in the provided text; only ‘normal subjects’ is stated). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract provided). Based on available abstract, this is a PET study of self-face recognition (passive and active recognition) in healthy volunteers. It does not target established executive-function domains (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility) and thus does not meet the review’s executive-function requirement. Inclusion/exclusion summary: Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none (cannot confirm from abstract). Inclusion IDs not met or not confirmed: I5 (not an executive-function task), I6 (within-participant contrast exists but not for an executive task vs active control), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise map cannot be confirmed from abstract), I9 (task not within established executive domains), I10 (participant age not reported in abstract). Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I5 and I9) is not met and the full text is incomplete, I exclude this study. If full text is provided showing the task actually probes an executive domain and reporting whole-brain group analyses and ages, inclusion could be reconsidered.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 20–44) that manipulates visual working memory load and attentional demand — a task within the executive function domain (working memory/attention). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., load 3 vs load 1; difficult vs easy search; interactions) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise statistical maps thresholded and reported in tables/figures (FDR-corrected). Imaging modality, participant demographics, health status, and task details are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses; not a between-group patient study; not rest-only baseline; empirical data present; participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, supplementary analyses).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical fMRI study of an executive function task (n-back working memory) in healthy adult participants (mean ages ~23–24) (I5, I9, I10). It includes within-subject task contrasts (3-back vs 1-back; error vs correct trials) comparing task conditions against an active control condition (1-back) (I6). Analyses are performed at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses and report peak coordinates and cluster results in tables and figures (I7, I8). Participant/sample details, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are described (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/rest, include within-group activation contrasts, and sample is healthy adults within 18–60 (no E3–E8 met). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study meets multiple inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI of an executive function (working memory) (I5), includes within-participant contrasts between active tasks (category vs location) (I6), reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses and statistical maps/tables (I7,I8), uses an established executive domain (working memory) (I9), and provides participant age, health screening, imaging modality, and task details (I10). However, it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes older adults (mean age ≈65.8) above the 18–60 age range, so the study includes participants outside the allowable age range. Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a verbal working memory task (an executive function domain) with healthy adult control participants. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (load levels > active control condition) and group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with reported activation foci/coordinates and descriptions of results. Imaging modality, task paradigm, and healthy control status are described. Although some detailed coordinate tables are noted as “available on request,” sufficient whole-brain results and within-group healthy-control contrasts are described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy activation maps, uses an active control, empirical human fMRI data, and participants are adults). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

Although this is an event-related fMRI study of a delayed-response task tapping working memory, action selection and planning (executive processes), with within-subject contrasts (specific vs non-specific preparation; reward vs no reward), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM results reported, the full text does not report participants’ ages or age range. Inclusion criterion I10 requires reporting of participant age (or age range) in addition to healthy status, imaging modality and task paradigm. Because participant age is not provided in the provided full text, I cannot verify that participants fall within the 18–60 healthy adult range, so I10 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered by the available content.

This fMRI study examined working memory (2-back) and recognition tasks in healthy adults, reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps, and provided participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task details (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, all primary activation contrasts reported are task versus fixation (rest) or task-related activation relative to fixation; no within-participant contrast against an active control condition is presented. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation used as the only baseline without an active control task). Full text is complete and reviewed in detail.

The paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults using an executive function paradigm (N Back working memory) with a within-subject Two Back vs Zero Back contrast and group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses. Whole-brain statistical maps and coordinates are reported for genotype group comparisons; imaging modality, paradigm, healthy sample status, and methods (scanner, sequence, preprocessing, statistical approach) are described. Although sample sizes are small in the fMRI subsamples, all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (task-based fMRI/PET of executive function; within-participant contrast vs active control; whole-brain group-level voxelwise results reported; coordinates/figures provided; tasks fall within executive domains; relevant participant, modality, and task information provided). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of an executive function (planning) task (Tower of London) in healthy adults. It reports within-participant contrasts (planning and movement execution vs four-move control conditions), employs group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction, and reports coordinates/figures and detailed methods/results. Participant age and healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not resting-state only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

Full text provided appears to be only title/abstract (fulltext_incomplete=true). Based on the abstract, the study meets I5 (PET task-based study of visuospatial working memory/executive control), I6 (within-participant contrasts between motor tasks and an active visual-detection control), I7 (group-level whole-brain PET analyses reported as task-evoked rCBF increases), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/regions), and I9 (task maps onto working memory/executive function). However I10 is not met from the provided content because participant age details are not reported in the supplied text (only “eight healthy subjects” is given). Because the supplied full text is incomplete, I cannot verify all required methodological details and participant information; per screening rules the incomplete full text prevents confirming all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria from E3–E8 are clearly met based on the available information.

Exclusion: E8 applies — participants are community-dwelling older adults aged 64–74, which is outside the required 18–60 healthy adult range. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not an fMRI or PET activation study; this is a structural MRI study correlating atrophy with behavior), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control neuroimaging contrast reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical activation maps), I8 (no task activation coordinates/whole-brain results to report), I9 (no task-based neuroimaging of executive function domains—only behavioral cognitive tests), I10 (does not report relevant fMRI/PET modality or task-based neuroimaging paradigm). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age 23 ±3) using numerical and physical Stroop tasks (executive function: conflict/inhibition). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; error vs correct) and models trial-by-trial pupil-related regressors. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed using SPM2 with voxelwise results reported and coordinate tables and figures provided. Participant health status, age, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain activation maps; not resting-state or connectivity-only; within-group task contrasts present; healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (students, N=14) using a size-congruity conflict paradigm tapping cognitive control/inhibition. It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs neutral vs congruent), group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with coordinates and figures, and describes participant sample, imaging modality, and task. Core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of conflict monitoring/resolution (executive control). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent; high vs. low conflict resolution) and group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper includes whole-brain exploratory analyses with FDR correction and reports activation coordinates and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The task falls squarely within executive function (inhibition/selective attention/conflict resolution). Participant age, healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting baseline only, empirical human data, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive control/executive function in healthy adults (n=16, ages 18–29). It includes within-participant contrasts isolating conflict (incongruent vs. congruent targets) and cue-related effects (cue-only vs cue-plus-target), and reports group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM'99 voxelwise ANOVA and thresholded maps) with coordinates and figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described in detail. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline, not a non-empirical paper, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met. Inclusion criteria met based on the abstract: I5 (PET task-based study assessing cognitive performance), I6 (within-participant contrasts including PMT vs an active motor control SHAM), I9 (task involves planning/visuospatial and rule-following processes consistent with executive domain). Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable from the provided content: I7 (cannot verify presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map from the abstract alone), I10 (participant ages not reported in the provided content; only ‘eight right-handed volunteers’ stated). Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and I10) cannot be confirmed and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending full-text review.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a minimal executive process ('refreshing') in healthy young adults (mean age 21.3), with clear task-based contrasts (Refresh vs Repeat) analyzed within-participants. Group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (Refresh > Repeat and Localizer contrasts), and coordinates/ROIs are provided. The task is explicitly framed as an executive/working-memory-related process (refreshing as a minimal executive function). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy young adults that directly manipulates executive-control components (working memory, selection, monitoring, stimulus–response mapping) using task-based paradigms. Within-subject contrasts (recency vs ordering, stimulus-number and response-number manipulations, recognition controls) are reported. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with tables of coordinates and figures are provided. Participants’ ages and healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are reported. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults using the antisaccade task, a well-established inhibition/cognitive-control paradigm. It includes within-subject contrasts (antisaccade vs prosaccade; correct vs error) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses with corrected thresholds and stereotaxic coordinates. Participant demographics (mean age, healthy status), imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. All required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an fMRI study of working memory in healthy adults (meets I5, I9) and reports group-level whole-brain multivariate (ST-PLS) results with tables/coordinates (meets I7 and I8), and provides participant demographics and imaging/task details (meets I10), the paper does not include a within-participant contrast of an executive-function task versus an active control in the reported analyses. Control trials were collected but excluded from the primary ST-PLS analyses (and no task-vs-control whole-brain contrasts are reported), so inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I6.

Excluded because the sample includes participants aged 37–83, i.e. includes individuals older than 60, violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task-based study of executive/cognitive-control processes using semantic and syllable decision tasks), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs an active control condition — semantic vs syllable), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described/figured), I9 (tasks map onto executive domains: working memory/monitoring/decision-making), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 satisfied). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded solely due to E8 (age range outside 18–60).

The study is a PET task-based study of random number generation vs an active counting control in volunteers, so it meets I5 (PET executive-function task), I6 (within-participant contrast RNG vs COUNT), and I9 (task falls within executive domains). However, only the abstract/metadata are provided (fulltext_incomplete=true), so I cannot verify whether a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map was reported (I7) nor find details on participant ages and explicit confirmation that the sample were healthy adults (I10). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be confirmed and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending full-text availability. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met from the abstract.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adult participants (n=12, ages 18–34). The study reports within-participant contrasts (Item-order vs Reordering conditions and parametric load effects) and group-level random-effects ‘map-wise’ analyses with contrasts yielding t-statistics (indicating voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI), participant health/age, and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within the 18–60 healthy range). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (visuospatial working memory and attention shifting). It includes within-participant contrasts (Rotation+Arrow vs. Rotation/Arrow; dual-task vs. single-task conditions) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects activation maps (coordinates, tables, and figures). The paper provides participant demographics (healthy adults aged 22–29), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and a detailed task paradigm. Reporting of whole-brain results and coordinates satisfies acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not exclusively connectivity/rest, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active control conditions, empirical with healthy adult sample). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16, ages 18–27) using task-based contrasts that probe rule maintenance/working memory and attentional control during categorization. Imaging modality and whole-brain, group-level SPM contrasts (CA vs FR, FR vs CA, and rest) are reported with cluster/coordinate data. The tasks engage executive processes (rule maintenance/working memory, target monitoring), and within-participant active-condition contrasts are presented. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. Therefore it meets fMRI/task-based executive-function criteria and provides whole-brain voxelwise results suitable for inclusion.

This study reports an event-related fMRI investigation of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). It includes within-subject contrasts sensitive to task phase and memory load (high load vs low load) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures. Participant demographics and healthy status (ages 18–28, n=15) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) are clearly reported. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (seven males, age 22–44) that directly probes working memory/stimulus discrimination (executive function) using a task-based, sequential two-alternative forced-choice paradigm. The paper reports within-subject contrasts isolating executive processes (P2 vs P1 for discrimination; P1 vs spheres for feature encoding) and models a delay period for short-term storage. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with thresholding and tables of Talairach coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting standards. Imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), participant demographics/health status, and detailed task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, includes active control contrasts, empirical data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

Although this is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and within-subject contrasts, it does not target established executive function domains. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrasts: introspection vs categorization; rapid vs slow), I7 (group-level whole-brain random-effects maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/figures), I10 (participant age, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported).
